- Foreign government 2017 report: no legal protection, trans people vulnerable to societal discrimination, stigma and violence limiting employment/education/healthcare.

Trans-specific violence in family/community sphere (corrective rape, forced marriage attempts) — that's resident-sphere mostly, but for a visitor the everyday exposure is societal discrimination + service refusal + no legal recourse.

Calibration: compare to 0.65 anchors — those have functioning remedies, documented acceptance. Here we lack working remedies (no GI anti-discrimination law, no hate-crime coverage, no enforcement record), but also lack tier-1 universal exposure and lack organized targeting.

Also strong positive signals: official endorsement at highest level, growing Pride, protective decrees for trans children/GBV victims, health policy non-discrimination on gender identity. That's more documented positive institutional climate than some 0.55 anchors.

But the absence of any gender-identity anti-discrimination law and hate-crime coverage, plus the 2017 foreign government report of societal discrimination and violence limiting access to health care — establishes a tier-3 societal hostility with thin recourse.

Where does this land? I think around 0.55-0.62. Negatives: no legal protection against discrimination, no GI hate crime, documented verbal abuse in medical/public services, family/community violence (mostly resident sphere), closed partnership recognition (tangential to visitors, mainly affects accompanying partners), unknowns at border/custody.

The 0.65 anchors have demonstrated remedies working — court compensation, prosecutions, enforcement. Here nothing documented working for gender identity. So below 0.65. The 0.55 anchors have recurring visitor-facing harms documented or partially corrected; here the documented harms are societal-level rather than a documented visiting-specific pattern. It's arguably a bit better than 0.55 given no documented pattern of service refusal targeting visitors plus strong official acceptance. But the total absence of any gender-identity legal recourse counts against.

I'd place ~0.58-0.60. Let me pick 0.58.

Under rule 13 ranking: known traveler-facing exposure = documented verbal abuse/discrimination in some public services (moderate, tier 3-ish, thin recourse); open questions (border, custody); resident gaps (no LGR, no anti-discrimination statute). No known good protections for the traveler specifically; but strong documented social acceptance at official level.

Hmm, "documented social acceptance of gender diversity" — Pride with 3000 participants and head of state endorsement, plus protective decrees. That's a positive. But reported day-to-day rejection too.

I think 0.60 is defensible. Let me settle at 0.58 — slightly below 0.60 boundary, still Reduced Risk band? 0.60+ is Reduced. 0.58 is Elevated Risk upper. Hmm.

This dossier lacks the equality law entirely but has no documented refusal pattern. 0.55-C has accepted culture, dead-letter statute, repeated harassment on buses — 0.55.

This dossier is comparable: accepted culture, no criminal law, some societal discrimination, no recourse mechanism. I'd say roughly equal, maybe slightly above because no documented visitor-facing harassment pattern and strong official endorsement. 0.58-0.62.

I'll go 0.60.

But not state-imposed; no documented ward-placement rule. So tier 3.

Final: 0.58. Hmm, or 0.60. Let me choose 0.58 to reflect the complete absence of gender-identity legal protection and documented hostility in services, while crediting the strong official acceptance.
